mainTopic: סוכה ישנה: must a סוכה be made לשם חג? The sources for בית שמאי and בית הלל, and the comparison to ציצית
overview: The משנה records a מחלוקת. בית שמאי say an old סוכה (built 30 or more days before סוכות, not for the חג) is פסול, and בית הלל say it is כשר. If it was built for the חג, it is כשר even if it was built a year earlier. The גמרא first gives בית שמאי the פסוק 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳'. It then shows that this פסוק teaches everyone that the סוכה's wood is forbidden for other uses all seven days, like the holy חגיגה offering. So בית שמאי's source moves to 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך'. בית הלל use that same פסוק to allow building a סוכה on חול המועד. בית שמאי follow רבי אליעזר, who forbids building on חול המועד. The גמרא then challenges בית הלל from שמואל's rule that ציצית must be spun לשמה. It answers that ציצית have an extra word, לך, that teaches לשם חובך. By סוכה, the word לך is used up to exclude a stolen סוכה, since ציצית have a separate פסוק ('ועשו להם') for that. So for בית הלל, a סוכה does not need to be made לשמה.

steps.title: The dispute over an old סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the מחלוקת: בית שמאי say an old סוכה is פסול, and בית הלל say it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An old סוכה: בית שמאי say it is unfit, and בית הלל say it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a disagreement about whether you may use an 'old' סוכה for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the two positions and no definition. The next line of the משנה will explain what counts as 'old'.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'old' סוכה, built well before the חג

phrases.english: MISHNAH: An old sukkah —
Beit Shammai deem it unfit
and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּכָּה יְשָׁנָה — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַכְשִׁירִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An old סוכה is פסול according to בית שמאי and כשר according to בית הלל.

steps.title: Defining an old סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines an old סוכה as one built 30 days or more before the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is a 'סוכה ישנה'? Any סוכה that a person built thirty days before the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what it means by an 'old' סוכה: one built 30 or more days before סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 30-day line matters because 30 days before a חג is when people start getting ready for it. A סוכה built earlier than that, with no stated purpose, is assumed to have been built for something else, like shade or storage.

keyTerms.meaning: And which one is it? (a formula that introduces a definition)

phrases.english: And which is an old sukkah?
Any that one made before the Festival
by thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term used in the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An old סוכה is one built 30 or more days before סוכות.

steps.title: A סוכה built for the חג is always valid
steps.stepSummary: If the סוכה was built specifically for the חג, it is כשר even if it was built at the start of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he built it for the sake of the Festival, even at the beginning of the year, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception: if you built the סוכה for the חג, it does not matter how early you built it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the real issue is not how old the סוכה is but what it was built for. Building it לשם חג removes the problem, and it is כשר even according to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of the Festival
From the beginning of the year

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think an early date by itself makes a סוכה פסול. Age only matters when there was no intent for the חג. Building it לשם חג makes it כשר even for בית שמאי.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת is only about a סוכה built 30+ days early without intent for the חג. If it was built לשם חג, everyone agrees it is כשר.

phrases.english: But if he made it for the sake of the Festival,
even from the beginning of the year — it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the definition of an old סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה built לשם חג is כשר no matter how early it was built.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why בית שמאי disqualify an old סוכה. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows a סוכה must be made for the חג.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for בית שמאי's ruling that an old סוכה is פסול.

steps.title: The פסוק requires a סוכה made for the חג
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn from 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳' that the סוכה must be made לשם חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'חג הסוכות, seven days to ה׳.' We need a סוכה made for the sake of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי read the פסוק as requiring a סוכה made for the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'חג הסוכות' link the סוכה to the חג. בית שמאי read this to mean the סוכה must be built for the חג, so a random old structure does not qualify.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"The festival of Sukkot, seven days to the Lord,"
we require a sukkah made for the sake of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַה׳״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'חג הסוכות... לה׳' teaches that a סוכה must be made לשם חג.

steps.title: What does בית הלל do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how בית הלל explain the same פסוק if they do not require לשם חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: the same פסוק exists for them too, so what do they learn from it? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the תורה is meant to teach something. If בית הלל do not learn 'לשם חג' from this פסוק, they must use it for some other lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: And בית הלל? (short for: what do they do with this verse?)

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel? (How do they use this verse?)

steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's position, which seems to ignore the פסוק בית שמאי rely on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק cannot go unused. If בית הלל do not derive לשם חג from it, they need to say what it teaches instead.

steps.title: בית הלל use the verse for רב ששת's rule
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל use the פסוק to teach that the wood of the סוכה is forbidden for other uses all seven days, as רב ששת says in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for רב ששת's teaching. רב ששת said in the name of רבי עקיבא: From where do we know that the wood of the סוכה is forbidden all seven days? The פסוק says: 'חג הסוכות, seven days to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית הלל use the פסוק for a different law: you may not take the סוכה's wood for other uses during the seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לה׳' gives the סוכה a status of being set aside for ה׳ for all seven days. So the פסוק is not about why the סוכה was built. It is about the סוכה becoming forbidden for personal use during the חג.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the verse) for something else

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that you may not take materials from a סוכה for personal use during סוכות.

phrases.english: That verse is needed for that of Rav Sheshet.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: As Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
From where do we know regarding the wood of the sukkah
that it is forbidden all seven days?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַה׳״,
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days to the Lord."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית הלל do not require לשם חג, the פסוק seemed to have no job for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית הלל, the פסוק teaches that the סוכה's wood is forbidden for other uses all seven days.

steps.title: The סוכה is holy like the חגיגה offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares the סוכה to the חגיגה offering: both carry 'שם שמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: Just as שם שמים rests on the חגיגה offering, so שם שמים rests on the סוכה, as it says: 'חג הסוכות, seven days to ה׳.' Just as the חגיגה is to ה׳, so the סוכה is to ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב ששת's rule by explaining why the סוכה becomes forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חג' here is read as the חגיגה offering, which is holy 'לה׳'. Since the same פסוק calls the סוכה 'לה׳', the סוכה also takes on a holy status. That is why its wood cannot be used for anything else during the חג.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of Heaven (a status of holiness)
The festival peace-offering brought on the חג
Just as... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חג' does not just mean 'holiday'. It means the חגיגה offering, which is why the comparison to holiness works.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי learn from 'חג הסוכות... לה׳' that a סוכה must be built לשם חג. בית הלל learn from it that the סוכה is holy 'לה׳' like the חגיגה, so its wood is forbidden for other uses all seven days.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַחֲגִיגָה,
phrases.english: Just as the name of Heaven takes effect on the festival offering,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַסּוּכָּה,
phrases.english: so the name of Heaven takes effect on the sukkah,
as it is stated: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days to the Lord";

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַג לַה׳ — אַף סוּכָּה לַה׳.
phrases.english: just as the festival offering is to the Lord, so too the sukkah is to the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains רב ששת's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the סוכה's wood is forbidden all seven days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירא comparing the סוכה to the חגיגה through the word 'לה׳'.

steps.title: בית שמאי also need that verse for the wood rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: בית שמאי also need the פסוק 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳' for the rule that the סוכה wood is forbidden. So how can they also use it for לשם חג?
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית שמאי also need this פסוק for that same lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the earlier answer around and challenges בית שמאי. If the פסוק teaches about the wood, בית שמאי need it for that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, בית הלל used the פסוק to teach that the סוכה wood is forbidden for seven days. Nobody argues on that rule, so בית שמאי must also learn it from this פסוק. A single פסוק normally cannot be 'used up' for two separate lessons, so the source for בית שמאי's לשם חג rule is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the פסוק) for a different lesson

phrases.english: But Beit Shammai also
phrases.notes: The challenge now points at בית שמאי.

phrases.english: need it (the verse) for this!
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule that the סוכה wood is forbidden, from Steps 7–8.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָמֵי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the lesson from Steps 7–8 to undercut the source given for בית שמאי in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5, where בית שמאי learn לשם חג from 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That פסוק is already needed for the rule that the wood is forbidden, which בית שמאי also hold. So it cannot also serve as their source for לשם חג.

steps.title: בית שמאי learn from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that בית שמאי use the first פסוק for the wood rule. It explains that their לשם חג rule comes from another פסוק: 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. Rather, what is בית שמאי's reason? Another פסוק is written: 'You shall make for yourself the festival of סוכות for seven days.' This teaches that we need a סוכה made for the sake of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge is correct. It replaces בית שמאי's source with a new פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (ויקרא) now belongs to the wood rule for everyone. בית שמאי's לשם חג rule moves to a second פסוק (דברים), which uses the word 'תעשה' (make). They read 'make the חג' as 'make the סוכה for the sake of the חג'.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (a concession)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two similar-sounding פסוקים here. 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳' (ויקרא) is now the source for the wood rule. 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים' (דברים) is the new source for לשם חג. The key word in the new פסוק is 'תעשה'.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
phrases.notes: The גמרא concedes that בית שמאי need the first פסוק for the wood rule.

phrases.english: rather, what is the reason of Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: The גמרא looks for a new source.

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
'The festival of Sukkot you shall make for yourself
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in דברים טז:יג.

phrases.english: for seven days,'
we require a sukkah made for the sake of the festival.
phrases.notes: This is בית שמאי's reading of 'make the חג'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the קשיא of Step 9 and moves בית שמאי's source to a different פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בית שמאי learned לשם חג from 'חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳'.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי learn it from 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים'. The first פסוק teaches the wood rule for everyone.

steps.title: בית הלל use the new פסוק to allow building on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בית הלל learn from the new פסוק. Its answer: you may build a סוכה on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? They need that פסוק to teach that you may make a סוכה on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly asks how בית הלל read the new פסוק and answers right away. They use it for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of a פסוק must teach something, so בית הלל must explain 'תעשה... שבעת ימים'. They read it as: the making of the סוכה can happen at any point during the seven days. That means you may build one on חול המועד, so they have no room to learn לשם חג from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of the festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel? (How do they use it?)
phrases.notes: The גמרא just asks 'And בית הלל?' It means: how do they use this?

phrases.english: They need that verse
to teach that one may make a sukkah during the intermediate days of the festival.
phrases.notes: 'Make it for seven days' means making it is allowed during any of the seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the earlier pattern (Steps 6–7): after giving בית שמאי a source, the גמרא explains how בית הלל use that same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps בית הלל should also learn לשם חג from 'תעשה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל use 'תעשה... שבעת ימים' to allow building a סוכה on חול המועד.

steps.title: בית שמאי follow רבי אליעזר, so the verse is free for them
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי do not need the חול המועד lesson, because they hold like רבי אליעזר that one may not build a סוכה on חול המועד. So for them, the פסוק is available to teach לשם חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי? They hold like רבי אליעזר, who said: one may not make a סוכה on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בית שמאי can use the פסוק for לשם חג. They reject the חול המועד lesson altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי also allowed building on חול המועד, the פסוק would be used up again. Because they follow רבי אליעזר's view that building on חול המועד is not allowed, they do not read the פסוק that way. This leaves 'תעשה' free for their לשם חג rule, and the two views end up neatly balanced.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold / are of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: פסוק 1 ('חג הסוכות שבעת ימים לה׳') teaches that the סוכה wood is forbidden for seven days, according to everyone. פסוק 2 ('חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים') splits the two sides. בית שמאי learn לשם חג from it, since they follow רבי אליעזר who forbids building on חול המועד. בית הלל learn from it that you may build a סוכה on חול המועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a מחלוקת about one law (לשם חג) can depend on a different מחלוקת (building on חול המועד). How each side reads the same פסוק is decided by what other lessons it must teach.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai? (How do they handle that?)
They hold like Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: one may not make a sukkah
during the intermediate days of the festival.
phrases.notes: So for בית שמאי, the פסוק is free to teach לשם חג.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סְבִירָא לְהוּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the obvious follow-up to Step 11: why בית שמאי do not need the פסוק for building on חול המועד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking בית שמאי to another תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי should also need 'תעשה' to permit building on חול המועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי follow רבי אליעזר, who forbids building on חול המועד, so 'תעשה' is free to teach לשם חג.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each side's reading of 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך שבעת ימים' is consistent: בית שמאי use it for לשם חג, and בית הלל use it to allow building on חול המועד.

steps.title: Don't בית הלל accept רב יהודה's rule about ציצית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge against בית הלל by quoting רב יהודה in the name of רב. ציצית made from leftover or hanging threads are פסולה, but ציצית made from balls of thread are כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And don't בית הלל hold like רב יהודה in the name of רב? רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If someone made ציצית from thorn-like leftover threads, from hanging sewing threads, or from the fringe-ends of a garment, they are invalid. If he made them from balls of thread, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new challenge against בית הלל by quoting a rule about ציצית. This step sets up the attack, and the full punch comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said a סוכה does not need to be built for the sake of the חג. The גמרא now brings a ציצית rule that suggests a מצוה object must be made with the מצוה in mind. Leftover threads that just happen to hang off a garment were never made for ציצית, so they are פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not hold (of this view)
Short thread-ends sticking out like thorns
Loose threads hanging down after sewing
Fringe-ends hanging from the bottom of a garment
Balls of thread, not spun for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: רב's own rule says the balls of thread are כשרה, so this quote alone does not yet prove anything about סוכה. The real challenge only works with שמואל's correction in the next step.

phrases.english: And do Beit Hillel not hold
the statement that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav?
For Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If one made them (the fringes) from thorn-like leftover threads
or from hanging threads or from the garment's fringe-ends, it is invalid.
If from balls of thread, it is valid,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל לֵית לְהוּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against בית הלל's view that a סוכה need not be made לשם חג.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that a סוכה does not need to be made for the sake of the מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel מצוה object, ציצית, seems to require being made for the מצוה. This step sets up that rule.

steps.title: שמואל's stricter view means the סוכה should also need לשמה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that שמואל said even balls of thread are פסולה, because the spinning must be done for the מצוה. So a סוכה should also have to be made for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: Even ציצית from balls of thread are invalid. This shows that we require the spinning to be done for the sake of the מצוה. So here too, we should require a סוכה made for the sake of the מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: This step completes the challenge. Since ציצית must be made for the מצוה starting from the spinning, the גמרא asks why a סוכה should not need the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל adds that even the spinning of the thread must be for the מצוה. That is a strong requirement of לשמה. The גמרא applies it to סוכה, which directly clashes with בית הלל, who allow an old סוכה built without the חג in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: For its sake, with the מצוה in mind

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: אַף מִן הַסִּיסִין נָמֵי פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: he said to me: even from balls of thread it is also invalid,
(evidently) because we require spinning for its sake.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי בָּעֵינַן סוּכָּה עֲשׂוּיָה לִשְׁמָהּ!
phrases.english: Here too, let us require a sukka made for its sake!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי בָּעֵינַן סוּכָּה עֲשׂוּיָה לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 13 by adding שמואל's stricter view.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that a סוכה does not need to be made לשם חג
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ציצית must be made לשמה, even at the spinning stage, then by comparison a סוכה should also have to be made לשמה.

steps.title: ציצית are different because of a special פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ציצית have their own פסוק, 'גדילים תעשה לך'. The word לך teaches 'for the sake of your obligation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'גדילים תעשה לך', 'Make fringes for yourself.' 'For yourself' means for the sake of your obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בית הלל. The לשמה rule for ציצית comes from a special word in the פסוק, so it is not a general rule for every מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that לשמה is a general rule for מצוה objects. The answer limits it: only ציצית have the word לך that teaches לשם חובך. Without such a word, a סוכה would not need it.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of your obligation

phrases.english: It is different there,
for the verse says: "You shall make for you fringes,"
"for you" means for the sake of your obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by tying the ציצית rule to a unique פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases with a special verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לשמה is a general requirement for all מצוה objects, including סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: לשמה for ציצית comes from the specific word לך in their פסוק, so it does not automatically apply to סוכה.

steps.title: The סוכה פסוק also says לך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the סוכה פסוק, 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך', has the same word לך. So it should also mean לשם חובך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the פסוק says: 'חג הסוכות תעשה לך', 'Make for yourself the festival of סוכות.' 'For yourself' should mean for the sake of your obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The סוכה has the very same word in its פסוק, so the same לשמה rule should apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer relied on the word לך. But that word also appears for סוכה, so the distinction seems to fall apart, and בית הלל are challenged again.

phrases.english: Here too: "You shall make for you the festival of Sukkot,"
"for you" should mean for the sake of your obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15 by showing that the same word appears by סוכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between ציצית and סוכה based on the word לך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word in the סוכה פסוק should teach the same לשם חובך requirement.

steps.title: For סוכה, לך excludes a stolen סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by סוכה, the word לך is needed to teach that a stolen סוכה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to exclude a stolen סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word לך by סוכה is already used for a different lesson: a stolen סוכה does not count. So it is not free to teach לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word teaches only one lesson. For סוכה, לך means 'your own,' which excludes a stolen סוכה. That leaves no word to teach לשם חובך, so בית הלל are safe for now.

phrases.english: That word is needed to exclude a stolen one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by assigning the word לך by סוכה to a different lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is already used for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לך by סוכה teaches לשם חובך, just like by ציצית.
steps.terutzMaskana: לך by סוכה is used to exclude a stolen סוכה, so it cannot teach לשמה.

steps.title: By ציצית too, לך should exclude stolen ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that by ציצית too, the word לך should be needed to exclude stolen ציצית. If so, where does the לשמה rule for ציצית come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, by ציצית, the word should be needed to exclude stolen ציצית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer around. If לך means 'not stolen' by סוכה, it should mean the same by ציצית, leaving no source for לשמה there either. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distinction between ציצית and סוכה rested on לך teaching different things in each place. This objection says the word should teach the same lesson in both places, so the difference between them is again unexplained.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole exchange tries to find why ציצית need לשמה but a סוכה (for בית הלל) does not. Each attempt to use the word לך to tell them apart is challenged, and the resolution continues next.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נָמֵי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי גְּזוּלָה!
phrases.english: There too, it should be needed to exclude a stolen one!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי גְּזוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17 by applying its logic back to ציצית, which undercuts step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that לך by ציצית teaches לשם חובך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If לך by סוכה teaches that a stolen one is excluded, then לך by ציצית should teach the same. That leaves no source for לשמה by ציצית.

steps.title: ציצית have a second פסוק that excludes stolen ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ציצית have another פסוק, 'ועשו להם', which teaches 'from their own' and excludes stolen ציצית. So the word לך by ציצית is free to teach לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, by ציצית, another פסוק is written: 'And they shall make for them', which means from their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18. It shows that ציצית have a separate פסוק to rule out stolen ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 asked: if the word לך by ציצית is needed to exclude stolen ציצית, where does לשמה come from? The answer is that the פסוק 'ועשו להם' ('for them', meaning from their own) already excludes stolen ציצית. So the word לך in 'גדילים תעשה לך' is not needed for that and can teach לשם חובך. By סוכה there is only one לך, and it is used to exclude a stolen סוכה, so there is no extra word to teach לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they shall make for them' (במדבר טו:לח), said about ציצית
from their own, meaning it must belong to them and not be stolen
there, referring here to the case of ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: ציצית have two פסוקים. 'ועשו להם' excludes stolen ציצית, and 'תעשה לך' teaches לשמה. סוכה has only one לך, which is used to exclude a stolen סוכה. So according to בית הלל, a סוכה does not need to be made לשמה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the same word must always teach the same lesson. The word לך appears by both ציצית and סוכה, but it teaches different things. By ציצית another פסוק already handles the 'stolen' rule, so לך is left free to teach לשמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why, according to שמואל, ציצית made from balls of thread are פסול, while according to בית הלל a סוכה built without intent for the חג (an old סוכה) is still כשרה.

phrases.english: There (by tzitzis), another verse is written:
phrases.notes: The answer is that ציצית have an additional source.

phrases.english: 'And they shall make for them' — meaning from their own.
phrases.notes: This excludes stolen ציצית, which frees up the word לך to teach לשמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the קשיא of Step 18 by pointing to a separate פסוק for stolen ציצית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional source. A second פסוק takes over one lesson, which frees up the original word for another lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the word לך by ציצית was needed to exclude stolen ציצית, leaving no source for לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ועשו להם' (from their own) excludes stolen ציצית. So לך in 'גדילים תעשה לך' teaches לשם חובך. By סוכה the single לך is used to exclude a stolen סוכה, so according to בית הלל a סוכה has no לשמה requirement. בית שמאי learn לשם חג separately from 'תעשה' (Step 10).
